goal: Test whether prefix-only low-risk early abstention can reduce total observation cost without increasing expected modeled loss over final240 waiting.
generator: SG052 unchanged synthetic 27 regime/sign configurations, 240-point continuation and unknown onset 100,120,140.

policy.candidate: Only if SG052 calibrated trailing100 HAC z=4.327111573414373 returns unresolved, allow early abstain (no forced directional commitment); otherwise observe and decide at n240.
policy.observable_feature: checkpoint:unresolved:|slope/se| band (<1,<2,<4,>=4):SE band high iff SE>=.002; no environment/true direction supplied to policy.
policy.training: 30 per sign-pair/noise configuration =810 traces, seed_start=215000000; for every unresolved checkpoint compare observed paired final240 loss against early abstain loss, sample cost .06, FP=150 FN=90 abstain=18.
policy.authorization: Group >=25 and empirical improvement mean - 1.64*sample_SD/sqrt(n)>0; choose first authorized checkpoint. This is a heuristic one-sided training bound, not a formal probability guarantee.
policy.note: Other checkpoint groups not authorized; no early directional commitment is allowed. At end follow frozen SG052 trailing100 decision.

pilot.disclosure: Training groups selected before pilot; pilot inspected, no change to thresholds or groups.

checks: Compare both policies on identical seeds
Decision loss as sample .06 each + wrong direction 150 + missed direction 90 + abstention 18
Record all modified decisions, wrong decisions and full replay ledger
Compare causal prefix replay and future-suffix perturbations
limitations: Heuristic training bound under fitted synthetic data, not rigorous generalization guarantee.
Early abstention changes the availability of late correct decisions; a lower modeled loss can still mean fewer correct directional outcomes.
Same family of simulated environments as SG052; no external robustness claims.
